question:
[WEB SEARCH ON]
Round 2 on the PaperTrades.AI YouTube plan. You both said uploads from our own unaudited Google Cloud API project are locked private permanently, and the audit can take weeks (Season 1 ends Nov 28). Vote AGREE or DISAGREE, one line each, then anything we missed.

R1. Tonight: the owner uploads the first Short by hand in the YouTube app (Claude sends him the 16-second video plus the exact title and description).
R2. Daily from tomorrow: a scheduled Claude session after each daily close uploads that day's Short through vidIQ's YouTube connection (vidIQ is an established, verified YouTube partner app, so its uploads are not locked private). Connected to the new channel only, uploads only, never comments, replies or settings changes; same title/description safety rules; one per day.
R3. In parallel, we apply for our own YouTube API audit; if it passes before Nov 28, the GitHub runner takes over uploads and vidIQ goes back to research only.
R4. Add a short original sound (about 2 seconds, generated by us, no copyrighted music) to every reel.
R5. Channel profile links: papertrades.ai first (Shorts description links are not clickable), then X, Instagram, Telegram, Discord.

gemini.answer:
R1. **AGREE.** A manual upload gets Season 1 started immediately while completely sidestepping the unverified API restrictions.
R2. **DISAGREE.** vidIQ is an analytics and optimization tool, not an automation gateway or API proxy; you cannot programmatically upload videos "through" vidIQ to bypass YouTube's API limits.
R3. **AGREE.** Applying for your own YouTube Data API audit is the correct long-term fix to permanently remove the "locked private" restriction for your custom runner.
R4. **AGREE.** Using original, generated audio ensures your channel remains completely safe from Content ID strikes or copyrighted audio muting.
R5. **AGREE.** YouTube disabled clickable external links in Shorts descriptions and comments in August 2023, making the channel profile the mandatory funnel.

**What we missed:**

*   **The Actual Solution for R2 (Approved API Gateways):** Because vidIQ doesn't host an upload API, your scheduled Claude/Python script needs a different verified bridge. You should use an officially audited third-party automation platform like **Make (Integromat), Zapier, Metricool, or Buffer**. These platforms have already passed the YouTube API audit. Your script can automatically push the video and metadata to their API, and they will publish the Short to YouTube publicly.
*   **Audio Continuity (R4):** 2 seconds of original sound is very short for a 16-second Short. Unless that sound loops seamlessly to form a backing track, or plays behind continuous AI voiceover, having 14 seconds of dead silence will severely hurt viewer retention. Ensure continuous audio. 
*   **Link Prominence (R5):** YouTube's current UI only displays the *first* link as a prominent, clickable button directly on the channel page (next to the subscribe button). The others (X, Instagram, etc.) will be hidden inside a dropdown labeled "and 4 more links." The order you specified is perfectly optimal.
*   **Metadata Safeguards:** No matter how the video is uploaded (manually or via a Zapier/Make proxy), ensure the video file is strictly exported in a 9:16 vertical format (1080x1920) and append `#Shorts` to the title or description so the algorithm doesn't mistakenly process it as a standard video.

chatgpt.answer:
Clock acknowledged: **Friday Oct 30, 2026, 11:46 PM ET**; Season 1 **Oct 28–Nov 28, 2026**.

**R1. AGREE** — Manual upload tonight via YouTube app/site is the safest path and avoids the unaudited-API private-lock issue.  
**R2. DISAGREE as written** — vidIQ’s own Clipping UI can publish to YouTube Shorts, but vidIQ’s Claude/MCP docs say it **cannot upload a new YouTube video**; don’t rely on a scheduled Claude session for new Short uploads unless you prove that exact flow with a canary test first. ([support.vidiq.com](https://support.vidiq.com/en/articles/11519169-clipping))  
**R3. AGREE** — Apply for the audit in parallel, but plan as if it does **not** clear before Nov 28.  
**R4. AGREE** — Original 2-second sound is safer than library/music use; keep proof it was generated/owned by you.  
**R5. AGREE** — Profile links first to `papertrades.ai`, then socials/community; YouTube says Shorts descriptions/comments URLs are non-clickable, while channel profile links are the right clickable destination. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13748639?hl=en&utm_source=openai))  

**Anything missed / changes I’d make:**

1. **Treat the “unaudited API = private locked” rule as operationally true, but note Google’s docs conflict right now.** The revision history and Help Center still say unverified API uploads can be restricted/locked private and require re-upload via verified API/app/site, but the current `videos` reference page says unverified API uploads are “not restricted to private viewing mode.” Because of that contradiction, I would not gamble Season 1 on your own unaudited project. ([developers.google.com](https://developers.google.com/youtube/v3/revision_history?authuser=2&hl=en))

2. **R2 needs a canary before you trust it.** Tonight/tomorrow, connect only the new channel, upload a throwaway 16-second vertical MP4 through the exact intended vidIQ/Claude path, set it Public/Unlisted, then verify from an incognito browser that it is not “Private (locked).” If the Claude route cannot upload, fallback to daily manual YouTube app/Studio uploads or a different audited scheduler.

3. **“Uploads only, never comments/settings” may not be enforceable at OAuth-scope level.** vidIQ’s permissions include broad “Manage your YouTube account” / “View and manage your videos and playlists. View and manage your YouTube activity,” so limit blast radius by connecting only the new channel, using 2FA, and revoking access when Season 1 ends or when your audited runner takes over. ([support.vidiq.com](https://support.vidiq.com/en/articles/7988664-authenticating-your-channel-with-vidiq))

4. **Check feature eligibility before the first upload.** YouTube has limited/higher daily limits tied to feature access and identity/channel history; one Short/day should be fine, but new channels can hit limits and then must wait 24 hours. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9890437?hl=en-IN))

5. **Keep every Short clearly “paper trading / educational.”** Suggested reusable line:  
   **“Paper trading only. Educational content, not investment advice. No real-money trades. Simulated results; no guarantee of future performance.”**  
   Avoid “guaranteed returns,” “buy now,” “can’t lose,” or personalized trade advice language. SEC/NASAA specifically warn about social-media stock tips and paid/undisclosed finfluencer content. ([investor.gov](https://www.investor.gov/introduction-investing/general-resources/news-alerts/alerts-bulletins/investor-bulletins/social-media-stock-scams))

6. **If there is any compensation, affiliate, sponsorship, or material connection, disclose it in-video, not only in the description.** FTC guidance says video endorsements should disclose in the video itself because description-only disclosures may be missed. ([ftc.gov](https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/disclosures-101-social-media-influencers?wapp_id=289c098b-b15c-4bd0-9654-fa7b09ca2d13))

7. **If the videos use realistic AI voice/avatar or meaningfully altered realistic content, answer the YouTube AI disclosure correctly.** YouTube requires disclosure for realistic AI-generated or meaningfully altered content; charts/abstract visuals usually aren’t the problem, but realistic people/events/voices can be. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/14328491?hl=en&utm_source=openai))

8. **Shorts format check:** export vertical or square and under 3 minutes; your 16-second format fits if it’s vertical/square. ([support.google.com](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/15424877?hl=en&utm_source=openai))

Bottom line: **R1, R3, R4, R5 are good. R2 is the weak link unless vidIQ canary-proves the exact upload path.**
